title: One chasing move and one idle move per cycle is not a perpetual chase
rationale: The rook attacks the unprotected cannon only from a3; on b3 it attacks neither a5 nor a6, so only every second Red move renews the attack while the cannon flees between a5 and a6. A perpetual chase requires every move the chasing side makes after the first of the three occurrences to renew the attack on one and the same piece, so a single idle move per cycle reduces the repetition to a neutral claimable draw; mx-chs-001 is the same shape with no idle move and is a loss.
